title: transactions savepoints retry execution strategies and concurrency
concepts: EF Core wraps a single SaveChanges call in a transaction when the provider supports transactions. Explicit transactions combine multiple operations but require correct lifetime and exception handling.
When SaveChanges runs inside an existing transaction, EF may create a savepoint; SQL Server MARS disables this behavior. A failed save can leave a transaction state requiring careful recovery.

Retrying execution strategies can replay database operations after transient failures. A manually controlled transaction must execute as a retriable unit, and a connection failure during commit can leave the commit outcome unknown.
Unknown outcomes require idempotency or verification, not blind retries. Generated keys, external side effects, and transaction boundaries affect whether replay is safe.
Optimistic concurrency conflicts are detected through tokens and require application-level resolution; retrying the same stale values does not resolve the conflict.
